transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-18 15:00 PST - Duration ~62 mins - Attendees: Priya, Luca, Maya, Tom, Avery, Jordan

Summary: quick internal launch readiness + incident review after yesterday's rollout triggered latency spikes on Redwood Dedicated. Focus: root cause hypotheses, immediate mitigations, and checklist for next canary.

[00:00] Priya (PM): okay, uh thanks everyone for jumping on. we wanted to keep this tight — uh, 45, 60 minutes ish — go over what happened in the rollout yesterday and confirm launch readiness items. Luca can you start with a quick incident recap?

[00:22] Luca (Eng): yeah, sure, so tl;dr: after we pushed the updated batching change and quantization switch to the dedicated pool, we saw a 3x increase in 95p latency for some p95/p99 tail requests for models with long context. it looks correlated with the batching window increase + a subset of requests hitting a KV cache miss pattern. i ran a couple quick repros but need to run a full bench.

[01:05] Maya (SWE): and just to add — logs showed some backpressure in the async queue, we've got a spike in queue length around 11:17 UTC which aligned with the customer traffic burst. a few pods spiked cpu and then evicted for a short period, which maybe amplified the tail.

[01:38] Tom (SRE): yeah i'm seeing the same in infra metrics. autoscaling didn't kick fast enough because we had a 30s cool-down plus the new batcher increased per-request processing time; so scaling lag + queueing = tail. also noticed some grpc retries which increased end-to-end time.

[02:10] Priya (PM): ok, so hypothesis list: batching window increase, kv cache miss pattern, autoscaler cooldown too long, and some pod churn. do we think it's a kernel/runtime regression or config tuning?

[02:35] Luca (Eng): likely config-heavy; i don't have evidence of a new kernel bug. the quantization path changed a bit but those ops are bounded. initial signal points to increased variance from batching plus cache invalidation. the kv cache miss case is interesting — there was a small change to key prefixing in the rollout which could cause misses for session-authored requests.

[03:10] Priya (PM): ok good. what do we want for immediate mitigation? revert the batching window? tighten autoscaling? revert the key-prefix change?

[03:30] Tom (SRE): immediate: revert batching window to previous default for the dedicated pool and lower cool-down to 15s for canary. that should drop queue length. second, enable more aggressive pod warm-up metrics so we don't get a cascade.

[04:05] Maya (SWE): +1 on reverting batching window. but i want to keep the quantization change in place while we validate — it's important for cost. if kv prefix is the cause, we should roll back that tiny change first if we can confirm.

[04:35] Priya (PM): action: roll back batching window now in canary, monitor 95/99p. Luca, can you run bench on canary with a mix that matches yesterday's traffic?

[04:50] Luca (Eng): yeah i'll run the bench, i'll use the load profile from prod replay — should have initial numbers within an hour, full suite by EOD tomorrow.

[05:12] Jordan (QA): i'll start creating a focused test in the QA harness that reproduces the kv miss pattern — it looks like session keys with longer context plus function-calling triggers it. i'll also add it as a blocking test for the deployment pipeline until we have confidence.

[05:40] Avery (Product Ops): i'll draft a quick internal comms note for sales/CS, short FAQ about what happened, what we reverted, and what customers should expect. we'll check with legal for anything external-facing.

[06:05] Priya (PM): good. timeline wise — Luca delivers bench results Monday morning, Tom updates runbook by Friday, Jordan updates QA by next week, Avery shares the comms today as a draft. sound about right?

[06:25] Tom (SRE): note: runbook needs explicit thresholds (eg p95 > 350ms sustained for 5 min -> rollback), and exact rollback steps. i'll add the metrics and playbook and tag the incident in the runbook repo. link: git.internal/redwood/runbooks/launch-rollbacks (will push PR).

[07:00] Luca (Eng): one more thing — we should consider tuning the autoscaler policy to account for heavier per-request CPU when batching is higher. right now the scaler watches CPU per-pod which lags; maybe also watch queue length or custom metric like pending_tokens.

[07:35] Maya (SWE): agree. also want to experiment with smaller max-batch sizes for long-context models only. we can have model-specific batch profiles instead of a global window tweak.

[08:02] Priya (PM): ok let's add that to the backlog: model-specific batching profiles and autoscaler metrics. prioritize post-launch but do a quick canary test next week.

[08:18] Jordan (QA): small note on tests: we saw occasional transcript/ASR glitches in the monitoring alerts that made triage slower — not relevant to infra but FYI for ops.

[08:36] Avery (Product Ops): curious — any competitive risk? did this cause visible customer complaints?

[08:44] Tom (SRE): we had two support tickets flagged internally and one slack message from a pilot customer. nothing public. CS handled initial outreach.

[09:01] Priya (PM): ok thanks. let's recap next steps: Luca runs bench and posts results, Tom updates runbook and cooldown policy, Jordan adds QA test, Avery drafts comms and notifies CS/SE, and Priya will coordinate a short follow-up on Monday to decide whether to re-run canary.

[09:30] Maya (SWE): one more operational ask — we should have a clear metric in the console for batch window vs tail latency so product can monitor. Luca can we get a dashboard tile?

[09:48] Luca (Eng): yes, i'll add a dashboard and share link. expect it in the same dashboard group as model-latency: dashboards.redwood.internal/d/model-latency

[10:05] Priya (PM): perfect. anything else?

[10:12] Tom (SRE): i'll also check the autoscaler logs for any anomalies last night and attach them to the postmortem.

[10:20] Priya (PM): ok thanks everyone. we'll reconvene Monday 10am PT if needed. meeting adjourned.

Action items (recap): Luca: benchmarks; Tom: runbook + autoscaler cooldown change; Jordan: QA test for kv miss; Avery: comms; Priya: follow-up Monday. Links referenced in call: docs.redwood.internal/launch-checklist, git.internal/redwood/runbooks/launch-rollbacks, dashboards.redwood.internal/d/model-latency.

Questions: - Should we permanently change batching defaults? not yet, more data. - Do we need an external customer advisory? not at the moment; monitor and escalate if more reports.

End of transcript.
